subject: Embeddings integration: next steps & migration checklist

Subject: Embeddings integration: next steps & migration checklist

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a migration plan scoped: 

Summary from call:
- Goal: Replace current embeddings provider for semantic search and recommendations (customer support KB + product recommendations).
- Volume: ~12M documents, daily delta ~50k new docs.
- Current vector dim: 768; Acme is evaluating 1024/1536 variants for better recall.
- Current infra: embeddings computed in-worker, stored in ElasticSearch with L2 similarity.

Action items I promised: 
1) High-level migration checklist and recommended batching/normalization settings (attached).
2) Notes on SDK auth and routing for hybrid setup (hosted + private inference).
3) Intro to our ML engineer (Vivek) to walk through vector dims and reranker setup.

Recommendations (short):
- Vector dim: start with 1024 for a balance of quality/cost; run an A/B eval vs 768 on a 100k subset.
- Normalization: we recommend unit L2 normalization at index time for cosine similarity; we also provide optional l2-normalized embeddings at inference to avoid double-normalization issues.
- Batching: use 512-2048 token batch sizes depending on payload; for document-embedding bulk backfills, use our async batch endpoint with 2k concurrency and chunk size ~5k documents per job.
- Migration: run shadow writes to Redwood index while keeping existing ES read path; once validated, switch reads and deprecate ES.

Next steps: 
- Can you share a short sample (10-20) documents and a small CSV of metadata? Ideally the acme-current-embeddings-stats.csv you mentioned.
- If okay, Vivek and Rishi can do a 45-min tech deep-dive next week to finalize batching and reranker params.

Attached: redwood-embeddings-migration-checklist.pdf (high-level steps + heuristics).

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Embeddings integration: next steps & migration checklist

Great questions, Alex — answering inline and adding details for the call: 

1) Cost & storage delta (quick numbers):
- Storage: 1024-dim float32 vectors are ~4KB each; 1536 is ~6KB. Storage increases linearly: moving 768->1024 ~33% increase, 768->1536 ~100% increase. If you compress/quantize (8-bit or 16-bit) we see ~3-4x storage reduction with minimal downstream impact for many retrieval tasks.
- Inference cost: relative cost per embedding call typically scales with model compute; if you use a larger model that outputs 1536 dims, expect 1.3x-1.6x cost per request vs a 768 model depending on architecture/sequence length. We'll share specific benchmark tables in the call.

2) Normalization:
- Recommended flow: normalize (unit L2) at index time AND store raw vectors (optional). At query time, return normalized vectors or normalize query emb before scoring. If your ES uses L2 and you switch to cosine similarity, converting to L2-normalized vectors is straightforward. The main gotcha is double-normalization: if you normalize twice you can degrade recall. We'll provide a small utility shim in the SDK to ensure consistent normalization.

3) Backfill & async batch:
- Our async batch job can write to either Redwood-managed vector index (recommended for ease + performance) or export output as per-document vectors (JSON/CSV) that you can push to ES. For migration, a common pattern is: run Redwood batch -> write vectors to S3/GS -> bulk-import to ES with your existing pipeline (we can help with an import template).

I've looped in Vivek for the model/dim/reranker specifics and Rishi to coordinate SDK/integration auth and routing (private vs hosted).

Proposed times for deep-dive: Wed 2026-11-25 10:00 PT or Thu 2026-11-26 14:00 PT. Which works?

Hi Alex — quick technical notes ahead of the deep-dive: 

Vector dims & reranker:
- Start with 1024 embeddings using a candidate reranker on top for high-precision reads (we've seen 6-8% absolute improvement on KB retrieval tasks vs 768 on similar datasets).
- If you need sub-100ms tail latency on retrieval, consider using lower-dim 768 for the first-pass ANN and rerank with a cross-encoder on top for the top-50 candidates. That hybrid gives good latency/cost tradeoffs.

Batching/backfill suggestions:
- For 12M docs: split into ~2500 jobs of ~5k docs each. Use Redwood async batch with concurrency=8 for fastest throughput without overloading transient infra. Output to S3 with manifest then import to ES via bulk API.
- Use per-batch dedupe keys (doc_id + source_hash) to avoid duplicate vectors if the job retries.

SDK/auth/routing notes:
- SDK: we have a simple python/node client. For private deployments you can use token-based auth with mTLS to our private control plane; for hosted flows we recommend short-lived API keys rotated via your KMS.
- Routing: if you want hybrid (some traffic private, some hosted), set routing rules in the console by tag (region, model-size). We'll provide a sample routing policy JSON in the call.

I'll bring a short perf table and an example backfill manifest to the call. Looking forward to Wed 11/25 10:00 PT unless you prefer the Thursday slot.

Cheers,
